A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Reconstruction Alignment by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original UMM post-training experiments, generation and editing evaluations, visual-understanding results, ablations and qualitative reconstructions.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds resolution, token-copying mitigation and training-dynamics analyses.

M1.justification: The reconstruction objective, combined losses, minimum-resolution rule and inference procedure remain unchanged. v3 Appendix E.2 implements a blur-based adaptation for Show-o's VQGAN variant by downsampling eightfold and upsampling; v1 Appendix E only suggested input perturbation as future work.

E1.justification: The training sources and task coverage are retained, including MidjourneyV6, LLaVA Mix-665K, FLUX-generated images, full/filtered BLIP3o-60k, and the generation, editing and understanding benchmarks. The new resolution and blurring studies vary reconstruction preprocessing within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The full comparator set from v1 Table 1 survives in v3 Table 9 despite the condensed main-text table. Editing comparators, qualitative ICEdit comparisons and SFT comparisons are also retained. Added encoder-resolution variants are experimental configurations rather than new comparison methods.

E3.justification: Reported BAGEL training data increase from 8,000 to 10,000 images, and Table 8 changes its batch specification from '8 (global)' to '8 (6 GPUs)' under per-GPU batch size. v3 also adds controlled resolution/blurring protocols and checkpoint evaluations through 10,000 steps. These substantially expand the experimental settings; the revised descriptions do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds BAGEL input-resolution ablation results in Table 7, quantitative Show-o token-copying mitigation tests in Figure 12, overall and subtask training trajectories beside Table 5 and in Figure 13, and a BAGEL distribution-mismatch case study in Figure 10. These substantially extend v1's existing encoder-type, training-order and leakage analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report twelve-seed evaluations for selected models. v3 Appendix D newly specifies seeds 0–11 and default seed 0 for other experiments. This adds seed disclosure without establishing increased repetitions; neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds resolution, blurring and training-trajectory outcomes. Between v1 Table 9 and v3 Table 10, OpenUni-1.6B's GenEval baseline changes from 70.4 to 56.0 while RECA remains 70.4, changing the reported gain from zero to 14.4. Harmon-0.5B's counting baseline changes from 57.8 to 55.8 without updating its +1.6 delta. The abstract's GEdit score becomes 7.27 instead of 7.25, matching v1 Table 3. Most headline benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A supplies mathematical background for autoregressive and masked prediction, diffusion transitions, flow matching and rectified-flow velocity. This expands formal definitions and derivations without adding a RECA theorem or proof. RECA's equations remain unchanged, and the CFG equation is relocated from Section 2.4 to Appendix B.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain caption-free semantic reconstruction, applicability across UMM architectures, efficient post-training and improved generation/editing. The abstract and introduction retain the same principal performance and generality claims. The shortened conclusion and expanded robustness emphasis do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explains higher-resolution conditioning through low-level shortcuts, interprets Show-o's resolution-dependent failures through token copying and pretraining mismatch, and connects BAGEL's dataset sensitivity to distribution mismatch. It also discusses subtask tradeoffs during training. These refine the existing semantic-alignment account; counting and BLIP3o limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds per-model training times, inference hardware, exact GPT evaluator versions, encoder input resolutions and dataset licenses. A new reproducibility statement promises code and weights without establishing their release. Documentation improves, although Appendix D's assertion that all training uses one A100 conflicts with Table 8's six-GPU BAGEL entry.

R1.justification: v3 expands supporting references and refines Section 2.3 with DEEM and VA-VAE, alongside new citations on feature reconstruction, NaViT, generation foundations and recent UMM/RL work. The established distinction between native reconstruction post-training and auxiliary reconstruction/alignment methods remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the motivation, method explanation and substantial experimental discussion, condenses the conclusion, and reorganizes the supplementary narrative into an overview and structured analysis subsections. CFG moves to the appendix, while background, reproducibility and LLM-use sections are introduced. This exceeds isolated copyediting.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the full main comparison table with a condensed version while retaining the full display in Appendix E.3. It adds a curve beside Table 5, expands Tables 7–8, introduces Figures 10–13, and rearranges retained qualitative figures. These substantially revise the evidence displays and layout.

improvement.justification: The resolution controls and token-copying mitigation tests strengthen support for the semantic-conditioning rationale and turn v1's speculative mitigation into tested guidance. More precise evaluator and implementation disclosures also help reproduction. These gains support a limited overall improvement, tempered by new reporting inconsistencies concerning BAGEL's GPU configuration and the revised counting baseline's unchanged delta.
